commitResults.messageBody: Move Remy's greeting, farewell, error, task-list, and task add/delete confirmation rendering into a dedicated Ui class. This keeps the command loop focused on orchestration while preserving the existing console transcript and task persistence behaviour.

Encapsulate Remy's mutable ArrayList in TaskList and delegate task addition, indexed access, removal, size checks, and task snapshots to it. Loading now replaces the task collection atomically, while UI rendering and persistence receive read-only task copies to keep the collection's mutation boundary explicit.

Move task-file loading, atomic saving, and saved-task deserialization from Remy into Storage. Add DateParser as a shared utility so command handling and persistence retain one authoritative set of supported date formats, while Remy only coordinates storage failures.

Move command recognition, task-index validation, and todo/deadline/event construction from Remy into Parser. Keep Remy responsible for command orchestration and task-list operations, while reducing CommandType to a pure command enum and preserving every existing command response.

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete Ui ownership of user-facing output
commitResults.messageBody: Move mark and unmark confirmations from Task to Ui, and route storage failure messages through Ui as well. Task now changes only its completion state, leaving Ui as the sole class that writes to the console while preserving message content and ordering.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move console input handling into Ui
commitResults.messageBody: Give Ui ownership of the Scanner lifecycle and expose a readCommand method for the application loop. Remy now coordinates commands without directly reading from or closing System.in, completing Ui's responsibility for console interaction.

Have Parser produce command objects that execute against TaskList, Ui, and Storage. Extract add, delete, list, mark/unmark, and exit behaviours from Remy's switch statement, leaving the application loop responsible only for parsing, execution, and exit control while preserving existing responses and persistence.

Task model: Assert task state invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
Task objects rely on descriptions and consistent endpoint data. Task lists also assume their elements and search terms are valid.

Assert these invariants so programming errors fail near their source. Add tests for the highest-value invalid states.

Command execution assumes loading always initializes the task list and parsing either returns a command or reports an invalid command. Parser helpers also expect only command types routed by their caller.

Assert these contracts to expose internal control-flow regressions.

GUI controllers rely on FXML injection and chatbot setup. Without that lifecycle, they fail later with less useful null errors.

Assert the required state at each boundary. Normalize the touched dialog property chain so the file satisfies Checkstyle.

The property-binding call places separators at the end of lines, which
violates the project coding standard and interrupts the fluent calls
reading order.

Move each separator to the beginning of its continuation line so the
layout follows the shared standard and passes Checkstyle.

Boolean-only exception constructors hide which command error they
represent, and the to-do overload accepts an unused parameter. This
makes parser call sites difficult to understand.

Replace those overloads with named factories and keep the existing
messages unchanged. Add focused tests so each factory formatting
contract remains explicit.

Saved-task parsing relies on raw character offsets and a long
structural condition. Those magic values obscure the file format and
make changes error-prone.

Name each persisted marker and boundary, and isolate status validation
before parsing details. Cover malformed type, status, and content
markers to preserve the tolerant loading contract.

Argument parsing slices messages using raw keyword lengths, so changing
a command name requires coordinating unrelated numeric literals. The
same command and delimiter text is also repeated across recognition and
parsing.

Name the command vocabulary once and derive all offsets from it. Add
coverage for each missing-argument path to guard the preserved parsing
behavior.

Task lists and search results duplicate their numbering loop and use
different spacing after the period. The divergence makes related output
look inconsistent and gives future changes two places to maintain.

Render numbered tasks through one helper and use the standard numbered
form in both contexts. Cover both views with exact-output tests.

Several command overrides repeat the inherited method contract, while
some summaries restate type declarations or implementation details.
These comments add noise and can drift from behavior.

Remove redundant override and inline comments, and keep concise class
descriptions that state purpose or rationale. Document the previously
undocumented launcher entry point.

The dialog layout uses an unexplained width multiplier and stores the
reversed children in a generic temporary variable. Readers must infer
both roles from surrounding statements.

Name the layout ratio and reversed collection so the binding and flip
operations communicate their intent directly.

Ui repeats the full divider literal in every framed response. This
duplicates presentation knowledge and allows individual messages to
drift if the divider changes.

Define the divider once and reuse it throughout Ui while preserving line
breaks. Add an exact farewell test to cover the refactored framing.

Deadline and event command methods validate syntax and construct
date-bearing tasks in one block. Mixing these abstraction levels pushes
both methods past the recommended size and obscures their happy path.

Move validated date conversion into named creation helpers. Exercise
date-time deadlines and date-only events to cover both helper branches.

commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks stay in insertion order, which obscures chronological priority.

Add a sort command for deadline due times and event start times.

Users need command guidance and a repeatable verification checklist.

Document the syntax and ordering behavior in both user guides. Add a
test plan covering automated and manual acceptance checks.

Profile pictures preserve their source aspect ratios, so non-square
user images do not fill the same bounds as Remy's square image.

Center-crop every profile picture and clip it to a consistent rounded
square. Keep the drop shadow outside the clip and cover crop geometry
with focused unit tests.

The user guide does not describe how profile pictures are presented.
Users therefore cannot tell whether image cropping is intentional.

Document the equal square presentation, rounded corners, center
cropping, and consistent styling of the initial greeting.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Recover from task file problems
commitResults.messageBody:
Task file failures surface as generic warnings, and malformed
records are skipped without telling the user.

Users need to know which data was recovered and why persistence
failed.

Represent load results and storage failures explicitly. Treat missing
files as a first run, report invalid lines, and translate read and write
failures into actionable messages.

Cover these cases with focused storage tests.

Storage failures are reduced to a fixed data/remy.txt message, while
malformed records are hidden from users.

This makes it difficult to repair a path or understand whether a
command remains available in the session.

Show the configured path, recovered line numbers, and session-only
save status in GUI and console responses. Place save warnings before
command confirmations so their order is unambiguous.

Cover the user-facing recovery behavior with integration and UI tests.

Task file recovery behavior is not documented.

Users and testers need to know how missing, malformed, and inaccessible
files affect task data.

Document first-run creation, malformed-record recovery, and permission
failures. Add manual scenarios so these environmental cases can be
verified in the JavaFX interface.

Impossible dates, invalid event ranges, and repeated task details can
enter the task list or saved data without a clear error.

These values create misleading schedules and ambiguous task records.

Parse dates strictly, require event starts to precede their ends, and
reject tasks whose type, description, and endpoints duplicate an
existing task. Apply the same rules while recovering saved records.

Cover the validation boundaries with unit and integration tests.

Input validation rules and their recovery effects are not documented.

Users need to know why task input is rejected and how invalid saved
records are handled.

Document strict dates, ordered event endpoints, and task uniqueness.
Add manual scenarios for command handling and saved-file recovery.

Commands with ambiguous spacing, repeated parameters, or unexpected
arguments can be partially interpreted as valid commands.

This makes user mistakes difficult to diagnose and risks executing a
different command than intended.

Validate spacing and command boundaries before parsing. Require
parameters to appear once and in order, restrict task indices to digits,
and preserve punctuation in free-form descriptions.

Cover accepted and rejected formats with parser and integration tests.

The supported command-format rules are not documented.

Users and testers need explicit examples of rejected whitespace,
parameter, and index formats.

Document strict command spacing, parameter placement, and numeric
indices. Add manual scenarios covering missing, repeated, and malformed
command parts.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tests: Cover application and console UI paths
commitResults.messageBody:
Application-level tests do not exercise the console loop, null input,
invalid task indices, or several console UI output paths.

These gaps leave user-visible command handling and stream lifecycle
behavior vulnerable to regressions.

Cover the command loop with isolated standard streams. Exercise bounds
errors, greetings, empty lists, task confirmations, and output-only UI
behavior.

Parser tests do not cover Unicode spacing, overflowing indices, mixed
event endpoint formats, or every missing-detail combination.

These branches determine whether malformed input receives the intended
actionable response.

Add cases for each unsupported representation and missing parameter.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tests: Cover storage recovery edge cases
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage tests cover common read and write failures but leave several
persisted-record shapes and load-result invariants unchecked.

Malformed records and leaked temporary files can undermine recovery
without affecting the happy path.

Exercise all supported endpoint representations, malformed delimiters,
failed replacement cleanup, null contracts, and immutable result data.

Task tests do not cover null collections and keywords or comparisons
across date-time endpoints and task types.

These cases define collection preconditions and duplicate detection.

Add focused assertions for null inputs and detail comparisons.

The build runs JUnit tests without measuring how much testable code they
exercise.

Coverage can regress silently as behavior changes.

Generate HTML and XML JaCoCo reports for non-GUI code. Make check
enforce 95 percent line and 90 percent branch coverage while excluding
JavaFX lifecycle code that requires manual testing.

Platform-dependent JavaFX behavior is not covered by the automated
suite.

Desktop differences in scaling, locale, input, and filesystem behavior
need repeatable manual checks.

Document the coverage boundary and a manual matrix for supported
operating systems, resolutions, language settings, and GUI lifecycle.
